summary: Any unseen position can contain a new minimum or maximum and change the answer, giving an Omega(n) inspection lower bound matched by the single scan.

optimality.argument: If an algorithm omits an array position, changing only that value to a new global minimum or maximum can change the chosen endpoint distance and therefore the answer. Every position must be considered in the worst case, and the implementation considers each once.

replacement_checks.evidence: An uninspected value can be replaced by a unique new extreme whose location changes the minimum swap count.
One loop performs constant-time comparisons and index updates per element, followed by constant-time arithmetic.
Authored cases cover one element, already-valid arrays, crossing and non-crossing extremes, duplicate minima and maxima, all-equal values, and reversed extremes.
